source: RFC 0007 §5.7 (DR1-F-6, RC review round 1 area F; design confirmed by the maintainer's coordinator, 2026-11-23)
statement: A document's max-count most recent revisions always keep their records, so a rollback to any of them works. All its records together, those included, weigh at most max-count times the document cap (400 MB by default; each record is at most the cap, so the most recent alone never pass it, and when they are all at the cap no older record stays), and beyond them its revision index lists at most the cap at 320 bytes an entry (26,214 entries by default), since the index is one stored value read and written twice a publish. Past either, a reclamation removes the oldest first, younger than cosec.control.revisions.min-age or not, except a record an open change rests on and the head; each record so removed within min-age is counted (cosec.control.revisions.reclaimed-young) and warned of, at most once a reclaim pass. An index entry names its record's stored size; one an older version wrote is sized from its record once. The records, their bytes and the open changes are metered by the pass that holds the reclaim lease, which replaces them when it ends and reports the last pass's until then; an instance another one led the pass for reports 0, and one whose pass could not start keeps what it last found, so the largest across instances is the store's.
